thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected for customer AegisLabs on Dedicated cluster eu-central-1a. 5m error rate 12% (baseline 0.6%). Alert: dedicated.tenant.5xx_rate > 5% for 3m.

sam (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking routing. assigning priority: P1.

priya (sre): thanks Sam. quick checks: is this KV eviction related or GPU queue saturation? either shows similar symptom. Mateo, any ongoing deploys to eu-central-1a?

mateo (runtime): no scheduled deploys. infra deploy bot shows no new builds in last 6h. I'm seeing a spike in inflight requests to tenant id aegislabs-47 — qlen up 8x. KV eviction rate for their shard is elevated.

anya (support): I'm opening a line with AegisLabs: Kevin, can you confirm if they're seeing errors?

kevin (cs): pinged them on the support channel. they report "gateway errors and intermittent timeouts for background inference calls" and one internal job started spiking retries at ~09:03 UTC.

priya (sre): Okay likely noisy neighbor or runaway job. Sam – can you run this to confirm inflight per-tenant?

sam (oncall): running quick query: `select tenant_id, avg(inflight), p95(latency), 5xx_rate from metrics where cluster='eu-central-1a' group by tenant_id order by inflight desc limit 10;`

sam (oncall): results: aegislabs-47 inflight=620 (norm ~40), 5xx_rate=11.8%, p95=2.4s. next highest tenant inflight=95.

mateo (runtime): That's definitely saturating actor pools. KV cache misses for that tenant jumped too — their model uses large KV working set, looks like their job bumped sequence lengths. Could be a batch job.

priya (sre): mitigation options: 1) Instant tenant-level concurrency cap (shed). 2) Evict long-running KV entries for that tenant. 3) Temporarily reroute that tenant to lower-concurrency / smaller model variant or hosted fallback. Any preference?

sam (oncall): prefer non-intrusive first: apply concurrency cap (1) and route to fallback if still bad. Mateo can you apply per-tenant cap?

mateo (runtime): I can flip the per-tenant concurrency policy for aegislabs-47 to 2 -> 1. will also enable token-budget shedding. Doing now.

deploy-bot: Executing policy change: `PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/aegislabs-47/policy` payload: `{ "max_concurrency": 1, "token_budget_pct": 0.1 }` — succeeded.

sam (oncall): monitoring...

priya (sre): I'm also kicking off a targeted eviction for that tenant's KV shard to clear thrash. Mateo, please confirm safe window.

mateo (runtime): safe. running `curl -XPOST https://internal-api/dedicated/evict?k=tenant:aegislabs-47&shard=eu-central-1a` — eviction started.

nora (mlops): FYI I see the tenant has 3 large long-running generation jobs started at 08:59 UTC (high token limits). Asking AegisLabs if they kicked off batch scoring.

AegisLabs (customer): yes we launched a bulk scoring run accidentally with max_tokens=65536, finishing up now. apologies. seeing timeouts.

kevin (cs): got confirmation. asked them to pause remaining jobs.

sam (oncall): great — eviction in progress. checking 5xx now.

sam (oncall): 2m after cap: 5xx rate down to 4.2%, inflight -> 58. latency p95 -> 720ms. improvement but not fully back to baseline.

priya (sre): nice. Can we also spin up a standby shard for tenant while they finish their backfill? Adds capacity and isolates load.

mateo (runtime): I can provision an ephemeral node pool dedicated to aegislabs-47 in cluster eu-central-1a or migrate them to eu-central-1b. Provisioning ephemeral pool takes ~3-4m. Migration to another cluster requires routing change and tenant pin update, ~6-10m. Which do we want?

sam (oncall): let's do ephemeral pool in same cluster for fastest isolation. Mateo, proceed.

mateo (runtime): provisioning GPU nodes + runtime containers. `k8s create nodepool --name=ephemeral-aegis-5761 --size=3gpus --region=eu-central-1a` — started.

deploy-bot: Nodepool creation in progress (job id np-88312).

priya (sre): I'll watch KV metrics and request queue. Sam, can you update the incident channel with customer impact statement for postmortem?

sam (oncall): Drafting: "Between 09:03-09:12 UTC AegisLabs triggered an unintended high-volume scoring job on Dedicated cluster eu-central-1a (tenant aegislabs-47) which caused KV cache thrash and inflight queue saturation. Result: elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts affecting only that tenant and transiently raising cluster error surface. Immediate mitigations: per-tenant concurrency cap, targeted KV eviction, ephemeral nodepool provisioning, and coordination with customer to pause job. No other tenants materially impacted." Thoughts?

anya (support): add note: customer saw ~30% of their calls 5xx during spike window; they retried causing some duplicate work.

kevin (cs): adding: customer wants ETA for recurrence prevention and if we can provide a soft limit in their account.

nora (mlops): follow-ups: 1) recommend account-level soft token cap and auto-shedding for future large batch jobs. 2) add guardrails in Console to warn when max_tokens > 8192 for dedicated tenants.

sam (oncall): agreed. Priya will own short-term mitigations; Mateo and Nora will own follow-up changes. I'll note owners in the incident doc.

priya (sre): checking current numbers: 5xx rate now 0.8% and trending down. Nodepool is healthy; new instances registered and some traffic draining to them.

mateo (runtime): ephemeral pool ready and routing shifted. `tenant-route --set aegislabs-47 pool=ephemeral-aegis-5761` succeeded.

sam (oncall): customer confirmed they paused the job and error rate dropped on their side. AegisLabs: can you confirm end-to-end?

AegisLabs (customer): confirmed. errors dropped to near 0 after pause. thanks for fast response.

priya (sre): marking incident as mitigated. we'll keep monitoring for 30 minutes before close. please file postmortem template with timeline, impact, and action items: add soft token cap, console warning, auto-evict heuristics, and per-tenant backpressure alert thresholds.

sam (oncall): capturing timeline and owners now. closing update in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
